newsitem.title: CHINA: Guangdong Power plans 100 mln new B shrs.
newsitem.headline: Guangdong Power plans 100 mln new B shrs.

text.p: Guangdong Electric Power Development Co Ltd plans to make an offer of 100 million new B shares to raise about HK$600 million later this year, company spokesman Cheng Chuyang said on Monday.
The company would use the proceeds to finance an expansion of its 51 percent-owned Zhanjiang power plant, Cheng told the Hong Kong-based newsletter the China Securities Bulletin.
Earlier this year, the company said it planned to double the number of the plant's generators to four, each with 300,000 kw capacity.
The expansion would need a total investment of 3.2 billion yuan ($385.5 million), with the third generator expected to start operation by 1999 and the fourth the following year, it said.
The firm planned to appoint China Southern Securities Co Ltd as the chief domestic underwriter and Nomura International (HK) Ltd the global coordinator, Cheng said.
Guangdong Power has filed an application on the issue with the Guangdong Securities Regulatory Commission, Cheng said, adding final approval must be given by regulators in Beijing.

The power supplier's net profits for the first half of 1997 were little changed from 296.10 million yuan in the year-earlier period under international accounting standards because electricity output and rates remained unchanged, Cheng said.
The firm would release interim results to the public in mid-August, he said.
The company posted net profits of 563.75 million yuan for 1996, compared with 376.97 million the previous year based on international standards.

The company had 825.45 million shares outstanding at end-1996, consisting of 513.65 million non-listed shares, 98.55 million domestic currency A shares and 213.25 million hard currency B shares, according to the firm's 1996 annual report.
